_doc: Per-indicator FETCH specs for the Pressure layer — what scripts/fetch-pressure-observations.mjs pulls to compute each indicator's window % change. Mirrors data/cost-index-sources.json: every spec carries `verified`. EIA/USDM/NWS specs are VERIFIED (stable series id / keyless REST). NASS specs carry an exact `short_desc` so the API returns ONE clean series — nassSeries flattens every returned row into one sorted array, so a query matching multiple short_desc/unit_desc values interleaves several series and windowChange returns garbage. Pin short_desc, confirm the change in --probe, then go live. Keys (free): EIA_KEY, NASS_KEY. USDM + NWS are keyless. scripts/check-pressure-sources.mjs validates shape + manifest alignment and reports readiness.

diesel.note: Weekly U.S. No. 2 diesel retail (EIA Open Data v2). VERIFIED series id. Probe: rows=1682 change=-7.6%.

drought-ca-az.note: US Drought Monitor REST, CA+AZ state FIPS, severe-area share. Keyless. Endpoint returns CSV unless Accept: application/json is sent (fetcher sets it).

drought-fl-ca.note: FL+CA severe-area share. Keyless. Accept: application/json (fetcher sets it).

drought-id._verify: Idaho (FIPS 16) severe-area share for russet potatoes — identical keyless mechanism to drought-ca-az/fl-ca (which return data), just a different aoi. Confirm in --probe (expect rows≈22, a sane % change), then flip.

drought._verify: aoi=US returns empty from the StateStatistics endpoint — national needs the USStatistics/GetDroughtSeverityStatisticsByArea path, not StateStatistics. Confirm the national endpoint before flipping. The two state specs already cover the CA/AZ/FL produce zones.

freeze-alert.note: Active freeze warnings over the winter growing zones (api.weather.gov). Keyless; encodes active=+1. Probe: rows=1.

feed-grain._verify: Global corn price (IMF via FRED, monthly) as the feed-cost proxy — feed is 60-70% of meat/dairy cost, and the old AMS feed-futures was a narrative report (dead). Needs FRED_KEY (free, fredaccount.stlouisfed.org). Probe to confirm the series resolves + a sane monthly change, then flip. Soy-meal (PSMEAUSDM) blend is a documented fast-follow.

imf-salmon-price._verify: IMF Global price of Fish/Salmon (index, monthly, via FRED). The INTERNATIONAL leading indicator for salmon-fillet: ~70% of US salmon is imported (Chile/Norway/Canada), so the world farmed-salmon price leads the US import/wholesale cost as cargoes land (~1-3 mo). Mirrors data/cost-index-sources.json salmon-fillet.fred. Needs FRED_KEY. Probe to confirm + a sane monthly change, then flip.

imf-shrimp-price._verify: IMF Global price of Shrimp (index, monthly, via FRED). The INTERNATIONAL leading indicator for shrimp: ~90% of US shrimp is imported (Ecuador/India/Indonesia/Vietnam), so the world shrimp price leads US import cost. Mirrors data/cost-index-sources.json shrimp.fred. Needs FRED_KEY.

nok-fx._verify: Norway Krone per USD (FRED DEXNOUS, daily→monthly). Norway is ~50% of globally-traded farmed salmon; a STRONGER USD (DEXNOUS up = more NOK/USD) makes NOK-priced salmon cheaper in USD → US cost down (sign -1). Needs FRED_KEY. Probe, then flip.

feed-soymeal._verify: IMF Global price of Soybean Meal (index, monthly, via FRED). Aquaculture feed (farmed salmon + shrimp) is increasingly soy-based; feed cost leads the farmed price ~1-2 quarters. Also the documented blend partner for feed-grain. Needs FRED_KEY.

mxn-fx._verify: Mexican Peso per USD (FRED DEXMXUS, daily→monthly). Mexico dominates US winter produce (tomato/onion/romaine); convention is FOREIGN-per-USD, so DEXMXUS UP = peso weaker = cheaper Mexican produce in USD → US cost DOWN (sign -1). Short pass-through. Needs FRED_KEY.

aud-fx._verify: USD per Australian Dollar (FRED DEXUSAL — convention FLIPS vs DEXxxUS). Australia is a top US lean-trim/beef supplier; DEXUSAL UP = AUD stronger = US beef import cost UP (sign +1). Needs FRED_KEY.

nzd-fx._verify: USD per NZ Dollar (FRED DEXUSNZ — convention FLIPS). New Zealand is the marginal global dairy price-setter; DEXUSNZ UP = NZD stronger = US butterfat/cheese import cost UP (sign +1). GDT clears in USD so FX is partly pre-absorbed → incremental signal. Needs FRED_KEY.

inr-fx._verify: Indian Rupee per USD (FRED DEXINUS, daily→monthly). India is the FX-active top US shrimp supplier (Ecuador, the largest, is fully DOLLARIZED → no FX channel). DEXINUS UP = rupee weaker = cheaper Indian shrimp in USD → US cost DOWN (sign -1). Antidumping/tariff risk can dominate. Needs FRED_KEY.

deep-sea-freight._verify: US Deep Sea Freight Transportation PPI (FRED PCU483111483111, monthly, 1988+). A genuinely-free ocean-freight PRICE level (the named container/bulk indices — BDI/FBX/WCI — are all paywalled). Freight up → landed import cost up (sign +1) for everything that arrives by ship (salmon/shrimp/oils/cheese). Needs FRED_KEY.

salmon-norway-price._verify: Norway SSB PxWebApi v2 table 03024 — WEEKLY farmed-salmon export price (NOK/kg), 2000+, keyless. Norway is the global salmon price-setter, so its weekly export price leads US import/wholesale cost ~3-8 wk (sign +1) — a higher-resolution version of the monthly IMF index. SSB bot-blocks non-browser UAs; the fetcher sends a browser UA. Run `--ssb-discover` to confirm the table dims + that the price picker resolves, then flip.

salmon-export-volume._verify: Norway SSB table 03024 — WEEKLY farmed-salmon export volume (tonnes), 2000+, keyless. A genuinely-new SUPPLY signal: export volume up → global supply up → US cost down (sign -1), ~3-8 wk. Non-circular vs the US-PPI target. Confirm via `--ssb-discover`.

salmon-import-volume._verify: NOAA Fisheries FOSS trade API — monthly US salmon IMPORT volume (kilos) summed across all partner countries, HTS 030214/030313 (fresh/frozen) + 030441/030481 (fillet). ~70% of US salmon is imported, so import volume is a direct US-supply gauge: volume up → cost down (sign -1). Keyless ORDS REST, browser-UA. 2009+. Confirm via `--foss-discover`.

shrimp-import-volume._verify: NOAA Fisheries FOSS trade API — monthly US shrimp IMPORT volume (kilos), HTS 030617 (frozen warmwater) + 160521/160529 (prepared). ~90% of US shrimp is imported, so this is effectively the US supply series: volume up → cost down (sign -1). It is also the ONLY free structured shrimp source (Ecuador/India production is paywalled/PDF). Confirm via `--foss-discover`.

enso-oni._verify: NOAA CPC Oceanic Niño Index (oni.ascii.txt, keyless flat file, monthly SST anomaly 1950+). El Niño (positive ONI) warms the E. Pacific / Ecuador-Peru shrimp waters → disease (Vibrio/white-spot) + harvest disruption → tighter shrimp supply → cost UP (sign +1), ~1-4 mo. transform:level because ONI is an anomaly that crosses zero (pct change would explode). A regime gauge — shifts the odds, episodic. Keyless; no key needed.

eu-butter._verify: EU Agri-food Data Portal /dairy/prices (keyless, weekly). EU butter price (€/100kg) — EU is a marginal global butterfat exporter, so its price leads US import cost (sign +1, ~2-6 wk). Run `--eu-discover` to confirm the host + product/member codes.

eu-cheddar._verify: EU Agri-food Data Portal /dairy/prices — EU/Ireland cheddar price (€/100kg). Ireland is the EU's cheddar producer; price leads US cheese import cost (sign +1). Confirm host + that cheddar resolves for member IE (or EU) via `--eu-discover`.

sa-precip._verify: Open-Meteo ERA5 archive (keyless), daily precipitation over the Mato Grosso (Brazil) soy belt — a soil-moisture PROXY (soil_moisture is hourly-only in the archive). Dry grain-fill → lower soy/corn yield → feed cost up → meat cost up; precip UP → feed DOWN → cost DOWN (sign -1), ~2-8 mo. transform:level (deseasonalize → precip anomaly). A long-lead, diffuse feed signal.

ca-frost._verify: Open-Meteo ERA5 archive (keyless), daily min temperature over Yuma/Imperial (CA/AZ winter-lettuce zone). A hard freeze damages standing crop → price spike; min-temp UP → less freeze → cost DOWN (sign -1), days-weeks. A CALIBRATABLE version of the NWS freeze-alert (which the calibration skips). transform:level (deseasonalize → temp anomaly).

specs._movement_doc: ams-move specs pool Report Details rows from ALL active Daily Movement city reports (default list MOVEMENT_REPORTS in fetch-pressure-observations.mjs), filter to one commodity (exact), and EMIT three indicator observations — volume (national weekly lbs trend), imports (import-share trend), pace (trailing-4wk vs ~52wk-ago). The emitted ids are the rule indicators; the spec id (e.g. onion-movement) is not itself an indicator. Volume field is '1 lb units'; import flag is 'import/Export' (I=import). check-pressure-sources resolves emits → indicators.

onion-movement._verify: Probe (--probe) reports cities-hit, weeks, and the 3 emits. Confirm a sane volume change and non-null imports/pace, then flip. 'Onions, Dry' excludes Green/Processed/Seed via commodityExact.

lettuce-movement._verify: Romaine national movement. Imports likely low (mostly domestic CA/AZ) — import signal may be near-flat, which is fine.

tomato-movement._verify: Field/round tomatoes (exact 'Tomatoes' — Plum/Cherry/Grape are separate lines, matching the measured anchor). National pool fixes the single-origin Nogales seasonality; imports meaningful (Mexico via Nogales/McAllen).

potato-movement._verify: Fresh table potatoes (exact 'Potatoes' — excludes Seed/Chipper). Idaho Falls + others; mostly domestic.

specs._season_doc: Deterministic region-rotation flags (type 'season', keyless, verified by construction). Produce supply hands off between growing regions a few times a year; in those gap windows a soft shipment-volume reading is a PRICE EVENT, not routine (the Nov-2025 romaine spike: 20-lb shredded ~$23→$80 while national volume looked merely seasonally soft). The MM-DD windows are Muntin's illustrative encoding of documented USDA AMS shipping-point seasonality, not a USDA figure; revise as patterns shift. Returns +1 in-window (elevated spike risk → cost-up lean), 0 otherwise.

lettuce-transition.note: Romaine Salinas↔Yuma handoffs (fall + spring) — the recurring lettuce price-spike windows.

tomato-transition.note: Field tomato FL↔MX / domestic handoff windows (spring + fall).

potato-transition.note: Russet old-storage→new-crop gap (late summer), when storage runs thin before harvest.
